items.title: Cortical Labs unveils data centers powered by human brain cells

items.description: Australian biotech startup Cortical Labs announced Tuesday that it has unveiled the world's first biological data center in Melbourne and is building a second facility in Singapore, both powered not by conventional computer chips but by lab-grown human brain cells. The move represents a novel attempt to address the surging energy demands of artificial intelligence by turning to biology for computing power.

items.title: Oil nears $120 a barrel as Iran war sparks historic market surge

featured_image.name: Oil supertanker rates hit all-time high as Iran pledges to close the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Oil prices surged past $100 a barrel on Monday for the first time since 2022, as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran entered its second week with no signs of abating. Brent crude briefly touched nearly $120 per barrel before settling around $105, marking what Reuters described as the benchmark's largest single-day gain ever in both percentage and absolute terms. The spike sent shockwaves through global financial markets, with Asian stocks plunging and European equities hitting their lowest levels in more than two months.[1][2]

items.title: Oil tops $100 a barrel as Iran war chokes global supply

featured_image.name: Oil prices surge, but no panic yet, as Iran war continues - NPR

items.description:
The price of crude oil surged past $100 a barrel on Monday as the U.S.-led war in Iran entered its second week, sending gasoline prices sharply higher for American consumers and raising fears of a prolonged energy crisis rooted in the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude climbed to $103.74 per barrel on March 9, up nearly 12% from the previous trading day alone and roughly 50% higher than a month ago, according to Trading Economics. WTI crude oil futures spiked as high as $108 per barrel after Sunday evening's futures open, a historic jump from $72 at the start of the prior week. The national average for a gallon of regular gasoline reached $3.47 on Monday, according to AAA, up from $2.99 just one week earlier — a rise of about 48 cents in seven days.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: US rejects Iran's claim that warship sunk by torpedo was unarmed

featured_image.name: US submarine sinks Iranian warship off Sri Lanka killing at ...

items.description:
A U.S. Navy submarine torpedoed and sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean on March 4, killing at least 84 sailors in what marked the first American submarine attack on an enemy warship since World War II. Five days later, Washington and Tehran are locked in a dispute over whether the vessel was armed when it was struck, as the incident widens the U.S.-Israel-Iran conflict far beyond the Middle East.

The U.S. Indo-Pacific Command on Sunday rejected Iran's claim that the Dena was unarmed, calling the assertion "false" in a statement posted on X. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh had told reporters in New Delhi that the warship was "ceremonial" and "unarmed," saying it had been attending India's Milan 2026 naval exercise by invitation. An Indian Navy official, speaking anonymously, said the vessel was not "entirely unarmed".[1][2][3]

items.title: Kuwait's emir condemns Iran's 'brutal attack' in first address since strikes began

featured_image.name: Iran continues to strike Gulf infrastructure, hitting Kuwait ...

items.description:
Kuwait held military funerals on Monday for two interior ministry border security officers killed during ongoing Iranian strikes, as the country's leader broke his silence to condemn Tehran's assault on the Gulf state now entering its second week.

Lieutenant Colonel Abdullah Emad Al-Sharrah and Major Fahad Abdulaziz Al-Mejmed, both from the General Administration of Land Border Security, were buried at Sulaibikhat Cemetery in a ceremony led by First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef Al-Sabah. The Interior Ministry said the two men were "martyred at dawn" on Sunday but did not provide further details on the circumstances of their deaths.[1][2][3]

items.title: IAEA chief says Iran's enriched uranium likely survived strikes at Isfahan

featured_image.name: Meet IAEA chief Rafael Grossi: The man central to the Iran ...

items.description:
Nearly half of Iran's uranium enriched to 60% purity — just short of weapons-grade — appears to have survived months of military strikes, stored deep inside a tunnel complex at Isfahan that withstood the initial US-Israeli bombing campaign last June, the head of the United Nations nuclear watchdog said Monday.

Rafael Grossi, director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency, told reporters in Paris that his agency believes "slightly more than 200 kg, possibly a bit more" of 60% enriched uranium was at Isfahan at the time of the last IAEA inspection before the June 2025 strikes. That material, he said, is probably still there.[1]

"The prevailing assumption is that the material remains there. We have not observed — and not just us, but generally all observers utilizing satellite imagery and other methods to monitor the facility — any signs of movement that would suggest the material has been transferred," Grossi said, according to Reuters.[1]

items.title: IRGC vows only one-ton warheads, wider strikes as Iran-Israel war continues

featured_image.name: Iran's IRGC: Only one-ton warhead missiles from now

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared on Monday that it will exclusively launch missiles carrying warheads weighing over one ton, a move that threatens to intensify an already devastating conflict with the United States and Israel now entering its tenth day.

Brig. Gen. Majid Mousavi, commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, said the force and frequency of Iranian missile launches would increase and attacks would broaden in scope. "From now on, no missiles will be launched with warheads lighter than 1 ton," Mousavi said, according to remarks carried by Iran's state-run Islamic Republic News Agency. The announcement came hours after Mojtaba Khamenei was named Iran's new supreme leader following the killing of his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in US-Israeli strikes.[1][2][3][4]
